real_conflicts: Replacing the geometric silhouettes with 'grainy, double-exposure' photography (Visual Concept) would create a muddy, chaotic background that destroys the legibility of the headline. The current minimalist vector approach is the only way to ensure the text remains the primary anchor of the composition.

Shifting the title to the upper-left or upper-right quadrant (Composition) would break the visual symmetry of the road and houses, turning the poster into a generic 'Rule of Thirds' template. The centered placement is essential to the 'vanishing point' metaphor of the title.
accepted: Applying a subtle noise filter or texture overlay to the background (Color/Atmosphere) to break up the digital smoothness. This adds the necessary 'filmic' quality without compromising the clean vector lines of the text.
concession: I concede that the current serif typeface is too static and 'solid' for a film about disappearing places. It needs to be treated as a material that can degrade, rather than a permanent label.
compromise: Instead of replacing the imagery or moving the text, we will apply a vertical SVG mask or gradient to the headline 'WHERE THE HOUSES END' so that the letters fade or dissolve into the background, mirroring the visual treatment of the houses. Additionally, we will increase the letter-spacing (tracking) of the headline significantly to create a sense of distance and isolation, while keeping the centered alignment.
nonnegotiable: The headline must remain the dominant visual element, centered on the vanishing point, to anchor the composition and ensure the title is immediately legible.
